findings.claim: Generated Python debt collection now silently ignores ordinary orphan comments such as `# TODO: fix this`. countTodos previously counted these, but now delegates to a detector that recognizes only //, /*, and *. The Python checker explicitly scans .py files, so Python todoCount can report zero despite unresolved work. Support Python comment syntax before using this detector for its debt metric.

The scanner stops at the first comment opener without checking whether a block comment ends. Valid source such as `/* explanation */ const x = 1; // TODO: fix this` now returns no hits, whereas the previous gate detected the orphan. Resume scanning after a closing block comment so a later real comment cannot silently bypass both enforcement and debt collection.

Resetting quote state for every line misses real comments following multiline template literals. For example, in `const text = `hello` followed on the next line by `world`; // TODO: fix this` (with backticks delimiting the template), the closing backtick is treated as an opening quote and the TODO is ignored. The old gate detected this comment. Preserve lexical state across lines; the same issue affects generated Go code using multiline raw strings.
